tables/empty_strings_no.why: Upstream never applied EMPTY_STRINGS to SQLite imports (divergence: 'SQLite import string processing'), so a blank ' ' stayed; execsql2 stores NULL.

tables/trimmed.why: Upstream never applied TRIM_STRINGS to SQLite imports (divergence: 'SQLite import string processing'); execsql2 trims.

stdout.execsql2:
Warning: There is a potential un-substituted variable in the command
     WRITE "note outside=[!!~note!!] k=3" TO out.txt
stdout.why: execsql2 prints the 'potential un-substituted variable' warning on every such command, to stdout as 'Warning: …'. Upstream logs it, and prints it (to stderr, as '**** Warning …') only when write_warnings is on, which it is not by default. execsql2 bug: console output differs.

files/t.tex.why: Upstream wrote NULL as the word None in LaTeX (divergence: 'LaTeX export wrote NULL as the literal "None"'); execsql2 writes an empty cell.

files/t_schema.json.why: Upstream typed a text column holding dates as datetime from the strings' shape (divergence: 'DB-export type inference overrides source types'); execsql2 uses the driver's type, string.

tables/t.why: A column of decimals with different scales (1.50, 2, -3.25) is created as double upstream and decimal(3,2) in execsql2 (commit 9675d81, F-DATA-001, 2.22.0; not in the divergence record), so SQLite stores 2 as an integer, not 2.0. Undecided.

files/out.txt.execsql2:
until pass 1
until pass 2
until pass 3
i=5 j=3 k=3
files/out.txt.upstream:
until pass 1
until pass 2
until pass 3
i=5 j=3 k=5
files/out.txt.why: Upstream substitutes a LOOP condition's variables once, when the LOOP line runs; execsql2 substitutes them on every pass. A loop on a variable defined before it ran until BREAK upstream (k=5) and stops on the condition in execsql2 (k=3). Not in the divergence record. Undecided.

files/halt.txt.why: Upstream's WriteSpec.write passes substitute_all's (text, flag) tuple on as the text, so writing fails after the file is opened and ON ERROR_HALT WRITE … TO <file> leaves it empty; execsql2 writes the message.
